tasks.task: Come up with a batch of clearly different ad concepts

items.when: When you have an offer, a buyer and a proof list and need a batch of concepts with hooks and copy
When all you have is reviews and product facts and need one problem, one angle and a proof list
When ideas all come from one place, to draw concepts from seven groups and rank the best eight
When you want a wide grid of buyer types, angles and offers set out in test order
When a new batch is due, to write nine or more one-line concepts and make the strongest ones to look at
When a batch is drafted, to find concepts that are the same idea in different words
When every concept is a feature list and none has a simple idea a stranger would repeat

tasks.task: Pin down the buyer, awareness stage and angle

items.when: Before writing, to set how the ad opens, argues and asks for one named buyer
When you need to see which buyer, stage and theme cells have no ad yet and pick the next ten
When you have interviews, surveys or tickets and need the words buyers really use
When the product works for a reason buyers have not heard and it needs a name and a story
When the ad explains too much or too little for what this buyer already knows and wants

tasks.task: Write a hook bank for one offer

items.when: When you need fresh openings, or want to test hooks on a video or image that already works
When hooks all use one trick, to get openings from five tactics ranked by fit and proof
When the hooks are for video and must be checked for length and reading level
When you have a list of video hooks and must pick the few worth filming

tasks.task: Write ten ad copy variations for one offer

items.when: When each variation needs its own angle and copy inside the platform's limits
When you have reviews and facts and want a buyer brief, first lines and full copy in one run
Before writing, to choose a copy structure that fits what the buyer already knows
When the main line is flat, to get five short headlines that each take a new angle
When first lines are drafted, to score each out of 100 and fix the weak ones
When you cannot say which variation is being tested against which, or why

tasks.task: Rewrite a vague ad into a concrete one

items.when: When a draft sounds like every other ad and needs concrete lines and one clear ask
When an ad gets few replies and you need the likely causes ranked before rewriting
When the honest version might win, to try an ad that names a real weakness first
When a line is rewritten, to test it is specific, true and easy to picture
When the copy is adjectives and should be facts the buyer can check

tasks.task: Build ads from real customer reviews

items.when: When you have reviews and an org context and want a buyer brief, an angle and checked copy
When one review line is strong enough to be the whole image ad
When the reviews would work better spoken, to get a video script with a source for every line
Before a quote runs, to sort each claim into fine, needs proof or cut

tasks.task: Write a weekly batch of image ad concepts for a designer

items.when: When a designer needs a batch of image ads they can build without a meeting
When you need different ad patterns picked by buyer stage and proof, each with copy and layout
When you need three or four layouts with text zones and product placement to compare
When the idea needs more than one frame, to try it as a two to six card carousel
When a concept is picked and needs every word on and around the picture
Before the designer starts, to turn the strongest concepts into real-size mock-ups to compare
When an ad is mocked up, to score it against its page and get fixes and two rewrites

tasks.task: Write ads that put the offer first

items.when: When prices and deals are scattered, to find clashes and new offers worth leading with
When the offer is set, to get three different offer image ads in two sizes
When the chosen offer ads must go to a designer as a clear brief
When the offer ad is drafted, to check the offer is the first thing read

tasks.task: Write a short video ad script with a shot list

items.when: When you need hooks, a two-column script, on-screen text and a shot list for one ad
Before writing, to see four different kinds of script for this buyer and pick one
When a creator will speak it and it needs five timed parts from hook to call to action
When the script is approved and the editor needs timed shots and an edit list
When the script is drafted, to find each weak line with a fix and a score
Before filming, to check the ad still sells with the sound off

tasks.task: Tighten a draft video script before filming

items.when: When a client's draft runs long and needs cutting, a sound-off check and a viewer test
When the opening is the problem, to write several new hooks for the same body
After the cut, to confirm every line left earns its seconds

tasks.task: Plan a one-afternoon founder ad shoot

items.when: When a founder will film themselves and needs checked scripts and a plan for one afternoon
When you have hooks and stories and need a hook-by-body grid and a shoot list
When the shoot needs kit, locations, roles and timings written down
When each ad to be filmed still needs its script and on-screen text

tasks.task: Brief creators to film ads

items.when: When a script is approved and a creator needs a filming brief, shoot order and file names
When creators should get two or three hooks to try, not one fixed opening
Before the brief goes out, to check viewers will remember the brand and not only the creator

tasks.task: Tear down rival ads and report the gaps

items.when: When you have rivals' public ads and need a tagged table of offers, angles, hooks and proof
Monthly, or quarterly in slow markets, to rerun the teardown and refresh angles
When you only have rival names and need their live ads pulled from the public library
When you have an export and need counts by format, age and awareness stage
When rival ads must be grouped by theme to rank the gaps nobody is filling

tasks.task: Turn rival ads into ranked test briefs

items.when: When the client wants test briefs this week from a rival's library ads
When you want the gaps scored and a brief for each, to choose which to test first
When the client has a proven strength that rivals never state and it should lead the ad
Before a brief that names or compares a rival goes out, to catch claims you cannot stand behind

tasks.task: Plan a fair creative test

items.when: When you need one question, one change, a budget per version and a stop rule set in advance
When the test runs on Meta and needs campaign set-up, ad names and checks
When you must work out how many new ads a month the spend and hit rate call for
When tests run in rounds and each round should be planned from the last result
When a test changes three things at once and could not tell you why it won

tasks.task: Read creative test results from an export

items.when: When a test has ended, or the client asks which ads are working
When results must be read in order from attention to hold to click to sale
When a winner is called, to test for false winners and get keep, leave or replace calls
When the ads are video and you need each placed by hook and hold with a fix
When a whole campaign is weak and you must find the main bottleneck first

tasks.task: Plan remixes of a winning or tiring ad

items.when: When one ad is clearly beating the rest, or it is starting to fatigue
When one idea wins, to get ten to fifteen new angles on it with hooks and a test order
When a winner fades, to find the cause and get ranked revival moves and new hooks
When the best ad should be tried as a carousel or new still with every word unchanged
Twice a week, to catch tired ads early and get a brief for each

tasks.task: Check ads against platform rules and claims

items.when: Before any batch goes to an ad account, to catch lines and images likely to be rejected
When you need risks flagged line by line with safer rewrites
When the copy makes claims and each must be sorted into fine, needs proof or cut
When finished creative must be checked against the brief and the product facts

tasks.task: Run the weekly creative sprint

items.when: Weekly on a fixed day, to go from last week's results to this week's briefs
Before briefs, before images and before launch, to stop a sprint that is not ready
When the weekly quota of new ads is a guess and should come from spend and hit rate

tasks.task: Make ad images with an AI image tool

items.when: When you have a product photo and need settings and a prompt for each image in a batch
Before generating, to compare layouts so the batch is not one picture four times
When the image must carry readable words from the prompt
When images are being made, to build each ad at the placement's real size and compare them side by side
When images are back, to score each against its page before any go live

tasks.task: Check the ad and its landing page keep one promise

items.when: When an ad is ready, to score how well the page picks up its promise and rank mismatches
When the page makes claims the ad repeats, to catch ones likely to be rejected

always.when: Before any ad that must look or sound like the client: colours, fonts and voice from the live site
When copy states a number, result or comparison you cannot trace to the client's proof
Before a batch goes to a designer or an ad account, to catch typos and names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When the ads need campaign set-up, budgets and audiences, not only creative
When static concepts must be built into finished image files
When filmed clips need cutting, captions and exports for each placement
When the landing page behind the ad needs rewriting to match it
When the job is search ads with keywords and ad groups
When there are no reviews or interviews to build angles from and research must come first

gaps: No library item writes Google responsive search ad headlines and descriptions to character limits
No library item writes LinkedIn or B2B lead ad copy
No library item sets an ad naming convention so results can be read by concept, hook and format
No library item reads a creative export across platforms; the readers found are for Meta, TikTok or YouTube alone
No library item checks a creator brief for disclosure rules and usage rights
No library item offers clearly different creator briefs or shoot plans to compare
No library item turns one winning video into cut-downs for each placement and length
No library item checks AI-made ad images for wrong product details, warped text or look-alike faces
No library item scores a batch of static concepts before a designer builds them; the critic needs a finished ad
